slides.title: This stock almost cost me $80K
slides.body: Last week I almost bought it. My checklist stopped me. Here are the 5 checks I run before I buy ANY stock.

slides.title: 1. Can you explain it?
slides.body: If you can’t explain the company in simple terms, you don’t understand it enough to own it. Don’t buy it.

slides.title: 2. How do they make money?
slides.body: A great product is great. But if you can’t understand how they actually make money, don’t buy it.

slides.title: 3. Is it actually growing?
slides.body: Look at their revenue, their profitability, their margins. Is demand increasing or not?

slides.title: 4. What’s their moat?
slides.body: Why can’t other brands just swoop in and take their customers? Patents, better brand, better tech.

slides.title: 5. What could go wrong?
slides.body: Every company has a bear case: valuation, debt, competition, geopolitical issues. Most people forget that.

slides.title: No panic. A plan.
slides.body: When it goes sideways, you already know: add to the position, or get out early and protect your assets.

slides.title: Save this checklist
slides.body: Don’t matter if your mama, your cousin or I told you to buy. Checklist first. Tomorrow: the stocks I own.

slides.title: This stock almost cost me $80K
slides.body: Last week I was about to hit buy. Then I ran my checklist.

slides.title: Investing or gambling?
slides.body: If you don't check these 5 things before you buy a stock, you're gambling. Mama said buy? Cousin said buy? Checklist first.

slides.title: The 5 checks are up
slides.body: New reel is live. Watch it and save it before your next buy.
